Parks and Recreation Commission
  Special Meeting Agenda

  Tuesday, January 17, 2023

  4:00P.M.
  Legacy Park
  23500 Civic Center Way

The Parks and Recreation Commission will meet at Legacy Park, 23500 Civic Center Way at 4:00
P.M. The Commission will adjourn the meeting upon the conclusion of the tour.

Call to Order

Roll Call - Recording Secretary

Approval of Agenda

Report on Posting of Agenda - January 12, 2023

Public Comment

1.  Ceremonial/Presentations

  A.  Administration of Oath to Newly Appointed Commissioners

2.  New Business

  A.  Park Tour of Legacy Park, Ioki Property, and Malibu Bluffs Park

  Tour Site Itinerary

  4:00PM  Legacy Park- 23500 Civic Center Way, Amphitheatre

  4:30PM  Ioki Property - 23575 Civic Center Way, Civic Center Gate Entrance

  4:45 PM  Malibu Bluffs Park- 24250 Pacific Coast Hwy, Ocean Friendly Garden

  Note: Transportation will not be provided. Participants are encouraged to wear comfortable
  walking shoes and carpool.

  Recommended action: Tour Legacy Park, Ioki Property and Malibu Bluffs Park to receive
  updates on park projects by City staff.

  Staff contact: Acting Community Services Director Riesgo, 456-2489 ext.350.
   Adjournment

  Guide to the City Commission Proceedings
The Oral Communication portion of the agenda is for members of the public to present items which are
not listed on the agenda, but are under the subject matter jurisdiction of the Commission. Although no
action may be taken, the Commission and staff will follow up, at an appropriate time, on those items
needing response. Each speaker is limited to (3) three minutes. Time may be surrendered by deferring
(1) one minute to another speaker, not to exceed a total of (8) eight minutes. The speaker wishing to
defer time must be present when the item is heard. In order to be recognized and present an item, each
speaker must complete and submit to the Recording Secretary a Request to Speak form prior to the
beginning of the item being announced by the Chair (forms are available at the entrance to the meeting
room). Speakers are taken in the order slips are submitted.
Items in Consent Calendar Section A have already been considered by the Commission at a previous
meeting where the public was invited to comment, after which a decision was made. These items are not
subject to public discussion at this meeting because the vote taken at the previous meeting was final.
Resolutions concerning decisions made at previous meetings are for the purpose of memorializing the
decision to assure the accuracy of the findings, the prior vote, and any conditions imposed.
Items in Consent Calendar Section B have not been discussed previously by the Commission. If
discussion is desired, an item may be removed from the Consent Calendar for individual consideration.
Commissioners may indicate a negative or abstaining vote on any individual item by so declaring prior to
the vote on the motion to adopt the entire Consent Calendar. Items excluded from the Consent Calendar
will be taken up by the Commission following the action on the Consent Calendar. The Commission first
will take up the items for which public speaker requests have been submitted. Public speakers shall
follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.
Old Business items have appeared on previous agendas but have either been continued or tabled to this
meeting with no final action having been taken. Public comment shall follow the rules as set forth under
Oral Communication.
Items in New Business are items which are appearing for the first time for formal action.  Public
comment shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.
Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business described
above are on file in the Parks and Recreation Department, Malibu City Hall, 23825 Stuart Ranch Road,
Malibu, California and are available for public inspection during regular office hours which are 7:30
a.m. to 5:30 p.m., Monday through Thursday, and 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Friday. Written materials
distributed to the Commission within 72 hours of the Commission meeting are available for public
inspection immediately upon distribution (Government Code Section 54957.5(b)(2). Copies of staff
reports and written materials may be purchased for $0.10 per page. Pursuant to State law, this agenda
was posted at least 72 hours prior to the meeting.
 The City Hall phone number is (310) 456-2489. To contact City Hall using a telecommunication device
for the deaf (TDD), please call (800) 735-2929 and a California Relay Service operator will assist you.
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in
this meeting, please contact Environmental Sustainability Director Craig George, (310) 456-2489, ext.
229. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to
ensure accessibility to this meeting. [28 CFR 35.102-35.104 ADD Title II]. Requests for use of audio or
video equipment during a Commission meeting should be directed to Alex Montano at (310) 456-2489,
ext. 227, or amontano@malibucity.org before 12:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting.
I hereby certify under penalty of perjury, under the laws of the State of California, that the foregoing
agenda was posted in accordance with the applicable legal requirements. Dated this 12 th day of January
2023 at 2:00 p.m.

MINUTES
  PARKS AND RECREATION COMMISSION
  SPECIAL MEETING
  JANUARY 17, 2023
  LEGACY PARK
  4:00P.M.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Skophammer called the meeting to order at 4:09 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Dane Skophammer, Vice Chair Cayley Jenner; and Commissioners
  Georgia Goldfarb, Suzanne Guldimann, and Alicia Peak (an-ived at 4:33 p.m.)

  ALSO PRESENT: Kristin Riesgo, Acting Community Services Director; Chris Orosz,
  Recreation Supervisor; and Brittany Saleaumua, Administrative Assistant

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Guldimann moved, and Vice Chair Jenner seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0;
  Commissioner Peak absent.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Administrative Assistant Saleaumua reported the agenda for the meeting was
  posted on January 12, 2023.

PUBLIC COMMENT

  None.

ITEM I  CEREMONIAL/PRESENT ATIO NS

  A.  Administration of Oath to Newly Appointed Commissioners

  Administrative Assistant Saleaumua administered the Oath of Office to Vice Chair
  Jenner.

  Administrative Assistant Saleaumua stated Commissioner Peak notified staff she
  would be late to the meeting.

ITEM2  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Park Tour of Legacy Park, Ioki Property, and Malibu Bluffs Park
  4:00 p.m. - Legacy Park, 23500 Civic Center Way
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Special Meeting
  Minutes of January 17, 2023
  Page 2 of3

  Recreation Supervisor Orosz discussed the Legacy Park Rehabilitation and
  Revegetation Project. He stated staff had focused on native habitats and over 110
  bird species were identified at Legacy Park since June 2019.

  In response to Chair Skophammer, Acting Community Services Director Riesgo
  stated staff complete facility inspections daily and the number of homeless
  encampments had decreased in 2022.

  Recreation Supervisor Orosz stated Cathy Schoonmaker from the National Park
  Service verified the placement of the Legacy Park owl boxes were correct.

  In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Recreation Supervisor Orosz stated several
  trees struggled to survive in Legacy Park due to soil salinity.

Commissioner Peak arrived at 4:30 p.m.

  In response to Commissioner Peak, Recreation Supervisor Orosz stated the City
  worked with the Malibu Library to offer educational programs in spring 2023
  regarding Malibu's native habitats.

  4:35 p.m. - Ioki Property, 23575 Civic Center Way

  In response to Vice Chair Jenner, Acting Community Services Director Riesgo
  stated the Ioki property was 9.65 acres.

  Recreation Supervisor Orosz stated the property contained two entry gates and the
  City permits a maximum of six events per calendar year. He stated weed abatement
  was completed twice a year.

  In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Commissioner Peak stated she opposed
  installing native plants on the property until City Council provided direction on
  how they want to proceed with the site.

  Commissioner Guldimann discussed the history of the Ioki property. She stated the
  City should incorporate the Ioki name on future site plans and the Kapok and
  Jacaranda trees should remain on the property.

  5:30 p.m. - Malibu Bluffs Park, 24250 Pacific Coast Hwy

  Chair Skophammer stated the snack shack area and storage containers should
  include an art component.

  Acting Community Services Director Riesgo stated staff planned to meet with
  Councilmember Riggins, Commissioner Peak, and Malibu Little League board
  members to discuss the snack shack.
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Special Meeting
  Minutes of January 17, 2023
  Page 3 of3

  Commissioner Peak stated the park would need to be rezoned to allow food sales.
  She suggested reviewing all zoning on the vacant properties so the Planning
  Department could address it at one time.

  In response to Chair Skophammer, Commissioner Guldimann stated many
  residents were opposed to artificial turf.

  Acting Community Services Director Riesgo stated Malibu Little League installed
  new sod on the baseball infields.

  Recreation Supervisor Orosz stated the irrigation system at Malibu Bluffs Park
  baseball fields would be upgraded to improve full water coverage on the turf
  infields.

  In response to Chair Skophammer, Recreation Supervisor Orosz stated owls
  typically do not inhabit the owl boxes at Malibu Bluffs Park due to heavy foot
  traffic at the park.

ITEM I  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS (continued)

  A.  Administration of Oath to Newly Appointed Commissioners

  Administrative Assistant Saleaumua administered the Oath of Office to
  Commissioner Peak.

ADJOURNMENT

MOTION  At 5:55 p.m., Commissioner Guldimann moved, and Commissioner Peak seconded
  a motion to adjourn the meeting. The question was called, and the motion carried
  unanimously.
